# the lead copies it to crates/tessera-app-core/tests/fixtures/smart_selection_spec.txt). Nothing here was run in iTerm2;
# every expected span for section 3 was COMPUTED by tools/sim.py (Python `re`, iTerm2 scoring) from the rule table in
# section 2 and then eyeballed. Rows marked DECISION depend on a choice recorded in section 9.
#
# SECTIONS
#   1  how iTerm2 picks a match (scoring, precision weights, gestures)
#   2  default rule table (iTerm2 originals + Tessera additions), as RUST-regex-compatible patterns
#   3  double-click expansion table (strings; span = half-open [start,end) in CHARACTERS of the logical line)
#   4  cell-coordinate rows (wide characters, soft wraps, bounds)
#   5  trim_trailing_whitespace rows
#   6  copy semantics (plain vs with formatting, pasteboard types)
#   7  HTML and RTF grammar, escaping, caps, rows
#   8  S5 bounds table
#   9  decisions for the milestone lead, and issue-text corrections
#  10  sources

## 1. HOW iTerm2 PICKS A MATCH
# - Source: iTermTextExtractor.m `smartSelectionAt:withRules:...` and SmartSelectionController.m (gnachman/iTerm2 master).
# - For every rule, every regex match that COVERS the clicked character is a candidate. score = weight(precision) * length
#   in characters. The candidate with the highest score wins. No match at all => fall back to ordinary word selection.
# - Precision weights (SmartSelectionController.m L40-44): very_low 0.00001, low 0.001, normal 1.0, high 1000, very_high 1000000.
#   So one level is a factor of 1000 in score: a very_high match beats a normal one unless the normal one is >1000x longer.
#   Within one level the LONGER match wins. Tie on score: iTerm2 keys candidates by matched string in an NSDictionary and
#   sorts by score, so the winner of an exact tie is unspecified. TESSERA TIE-BREAK (DECISION D-TIE): higher precision,
#   then longer, then earlier start, then earlier rule in the list.
# - iTerm2 runs each regex on a text window of +-smartSelectionRadius lines around the click (default 10 lines, advanced
#   setting), restarting the search after each match START, so overlapping matches are found. Tessera: leftmost-first,
#   non-overlapping scan of a window of at most 8192 characters (S5); overlapping alternatives are not enumerated.
# - Quirk: iTerm2 matches against a substring that starts at the search offset, so `\b` and lookbehind see the substring start
#   as a boundary. Tessera matches against the whole window; word boundaries are real. Not a fixture row.
# - Gestures: iTerm2 double-click = word, triple-click = line, QUAD-click = smart selection; "Double-click performs smart
#   selection" (Settings > Pointer) moves smart selection to double-click. https://iterm2.com/documentation-smart-selection.html,
#   https://iterm2.com/3.3/documentation-preferences-pointer.html. Issue #47 wants double-click: see D-GESTURE.
# - iTerm2 ships a catch-all LOW rule `\S+` ("Word bounded by whitespace"). It makes smart selection never fall back to the
#   word. TESSERA DOES NOT SHIP IT (D-NOWORDRULE): otherwise `foo=bar&baz` would select whole and the existing word
#   tests (WORD_CHARS = alnum + `/-+\~_.`) would change, contradicting the issue's "word selection is unchanged".

## 2. DEFAULT RULES (Tessera). `pattern` is for the Rust `regex` crate: no lookaround, no backreferences; `\p{L}\p{N}` replace
#    ICU `[:letter:][:number:]`; `\w` below is NOT used for the path class. Precision names as in iTerm2.
#    Source column: iTerm2 = plists/SmartSelectionRules.plist (verbatim, modulo class translation); TESSERA = this fixture.
# id            precision  source   pattern
# cpp_namespace normal     iTerm2   (?:[A-Za-z0-9_]+::)+[A-Za-z0-9_]+
# path          normal     iTerm2   ~?/?(?:[\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}._-]+/+)+[\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}._-]+/?   (\p{M} added, #351: NFD accents)
# quoted        normal     iTerm2   @?"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"
# include_path  normal     iTerm2   (?:[\p{L}\p{N}._]+\.)+[\p{L}\p{N}._]+
# mailto        normal     iTerm2   \bmailto:(?:[a-z0-9A-Z_]+@)?(?:[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+\.)*[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+\b
# objc_selector high       iTerm2   @selector\([^)]+\)
# email         high       iTerm2   \b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,4}\b
# http_url      very_high  iTerm2*  https?://(?:[a-z0-9A-Z]+(?::[a-zA-Z0-9]+)?@)?(?:[a-z0-9A-Z][-a-z0-9A-Z]*\.)*[A-Za-z][-A-Za-z]*(?::[0-9]+)?(?:/[a-zA-Z0-9;/.\-_+%?&@=#~()]*)?
#     * iTerm2's real rule is two alternatives, the first guarded by the lookbehind (?<!\() so that `(url)` does not swallow
#       the closing paren; Rust regex has no lookbehind. RECOMMENDED: match the single alternative above, then apply
#       url.rs U4 (strip trailing . , ; : ! ? ' ") and U5 (balanced closers) to the span (DECISION D-URLRULE: or call url::url_at
#       directly, which also gives file:/ftp: and IRIs; the config rule then only matters for user rules).
#       Note iTerm2's own class INCLUDES `.` and `;` so it selects a trailing full stop; Tessera strips it (matches cmd-click).
# ssh_url       very_high  iTerm2   \bssh:(?:[a-z0-9A-Z_]+@)?(?:[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+\.)*[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+\b
# telnet_url    very_high  iTerm2   \btelnet:(?:[a-z0-9A-Z_]+@)?(?:[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+\.)*[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+\b
# --- Tessera additions: iTerm2 has NO default rule for hashes or IP addresses (issue text wrong, see section 9) ---
# git_sha       normal     TESSERA  \b(?:[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64}|[0-9a-f]{7,12})\b
#                                   normal, not high: a high sha would beat `deadbeef.txt` (include_path) and truncate a file name.
# ipv4          high       TESSERA  \b(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])\b
# ipv6          high       TESSERA  three alternatives, H = [0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}:
#                                   \b(?:H:){7}H\b
#                                   | \bH(?::H){0,6}::(?:H(?::H){0,6})?   (and the next char is not hex or ':'; Rust regex has no
#                                     lookahead: the implementer drops a match whose following char is hex or ':')
#                                   | ::(?:H(?::H){0,6})?                 (and the previous char is not alnum or ':'; same post-check)
#                                   Zone ids (`fe80::1%en0`), embedded IPv4 tails (`::ffff:1.2.3.4`) are NOT covered (D-IPV6).
# Order in the list matters only for the last tie-break. Not in the defaults: `\S+` word rule, single-quoted strings,
# Windows paths, line:column suffixes (`file.rs:12:3`), ports on IPs.

## 3. DOUBLE-CLICK EXPANSION TABLE (single logical line, no wraps; the click is on the char shown in `click`)
# Row layout:  ### <id> / text: "<line>" / click: <char index, 0-based> / expect: [start,end) "<span>" / by: <rule or word-fallback>
#              / note: / cite:
# "by: word" means the existing word_at behaviour (alnum + WORD_CHARS run, blank run, or one other char); those rows must
# equal the OLD result byte for byte (the issue's "existing selection tests unchanged").

note:   absolute path; click on its first char
cite:   SmartSelectionRules.plist 'Paths'; scoring: SmartSelectionController.m L40-44 + iTermTextExtractor.m smartSelectionAt

### SS-N6
text:   "[self perform:@selector(foo:bar:)];"
click:  10   # char "o"
expect: [6,13) "perform"
by:     word(word)
note:   click outside the selector: word fallback 'perform'
cite:   Obj-C selector; scoring: SmartSelectionController.m L40-44 + iTermTextExtractor.m smartSelectionAt

### SS-W1
text:   "foo=bar&baz"
click:  6   # char "r"
expect: [4,7) "bar"
by:     word(word)
note:   ':' '=' '&' end a word: existing word behaviour unchanged
cite:   WORD_CHARS in selection.rs; scoring: SmartSelectionController.m L40-44 + iTermTextExtractor.m smartSelectionAt

### SS-W2
text:   "a   b"
click:  3   # char " "
expect: [1,4) "   "
by:     word(space)
note:   blank run: existing whitespace-run behaviour, smart rules never match blanks
cite:   selection.rs class_of; scoring: SmartSelectionController.m L40-44 + iTermTextExtractor.m smartSelectionAt

### SS-W3
text:   "x ! y"
click:  2   # char "!"
expect: [2,3) "!"
by:     word(other)
note:   single other char
cite:   selection.rs class_of; scoring: SmartSelectionController.m L40-44 + iTermTextExtractor.m smartSelectionAt

### SS-W4
text:   "aaa bbb"
click:  3   # char " "
expect: [3,4) " "
by:     word(space)
note:   click on blank after word
cite:   selection.rs; scoring: SmartSelectionController.m L40-44 + iTermTextExtractor.m smartSelectionAt

### SS-W5
text:   "mid/dle-name_x.y"
click:  10   # char "m"
expect: [0,16) "mid/dle-name_x.y"
by:     path
note:   'mid/dle-name_x.y' by path (one slash)
cite:   Paths; scoring: SmartSelectionController.m L40-44 + iTermTextExtractor.m smartSelectionAt

## 4. CELL-COORDINATE ROWS (grid size RxC, 0-based (row,col), inclusive ends, as in selection_spec.txt `sel:` layout)
# Wide characters occupy two cells (WIDE + SPACER); a click on the spacer counts as a click on the wide char. Expected `sel:`
# is reported as clicked/ends, not widened (selection_spec.txt convention); extraction widens.

### SS-C1  (soft-wrapped URL)
size:   3x20
feed:   "see https://example.com/abcdef/ghijkl now"   # wraps after col 19: row0 "see https://example.", row1 "com/abcdef/ghijkl no", row2 "w"
click:  (1,3)
sel:    linear (0,4)-(1,16)
text:   "https://example.com/abcdef/ghijkl"
by:     http_url
note:   the rule scans the LOGICAL line (soft wraps join without a separator); a click on row 0 col 4 gives the same selection
cite:   issue #47 "scanned logical line"; selection_spec.notes.md U8 (soft wraps continue a URL); ADR 0009

### SS-C2  (wide chars before a path)
size:   2x20
feed:   "日本 /tmp/x ok"      # 日 c0-1, 本 c2-3, ' ' c4, '/' c5 t6 m7 p8 '/' c9 x c10
click:  (0,7)
sel:    linear (0,5)-(0,10)
text:   "/tmp/x"
by:     path
note:   columns, not characters, are what `sel:` counts; the wide chars shift col != char index
cite:   path rule; selection_spec.txt "reported as clicked"

### SS-C3  (click on the spacer half of a wide char: unchanged word behaviour)
size:   2x20
feed:   "日本 /tmp/x ok"
click:  (0,1)
sel:    linear (0,0)-(0,3)
text:   "日本"
by:     word
note:   non-ASCII alphanumerics are word chars today; no smart rule matches '日' (path needs a slash)
cite:   selection.rs class_of/word_at (existing tests)

### SS-C4  (wide chars INSIDE a path)
size:   2x20
feed:   "/tmp/日本/x ok"      # '/' c0 t1 m2 p3 '/' c4 日 c5-6 本 c7-8 '/' c9 x c10
click:  (0,6)                 # spacer of 日
sel:    linear (0,0)-(0,10)
text:   "/tmp/日本/x"
by:     path
cite:   path class \p{L}

### SS-C4b  (a decomposed (NFD) accent inside a path)  [#351 adversarial (5)]
size:   2x40
feed:   "ls a+/Users/Jose\u0301/cafe\u0301.txt ok"   # '/' c5; "e\u0301" one cell each (c15, c20); '.' c21, t22 x23 t24
click:  (0,19)                # 'f'
sel:    linear (0,5)-(0,24)
text:   "/Users/Jose\u0301/cafe\u0301.txt"
by:     path
note:   macOS file names are often NFD; without \p{M} in the path class the combining acute cuts the path after "Jose",
        and the click on "cafe" falls back to the word, "a+/Users/..." ('+' is a word character, not a path one)
cite:   path rule; UAX #44 General_Category M

### SS-C5  (match straddling the 8192-character scan window)  [DECISION D-WINDOW]
size:   2x200, one 100000-character logical line (soft wraps)
feed:   "a/" x 50000  (no spaces; the path rule would match all 100000 characters)
click:  a 'a' in the middle
sel:    the WORD at the click, not a truncated 8192-char path
note:   window = at most 4096 characters either side of the click. A candidate touching a window edge that is not the logical line's
        own start or end may be truncated, so it is dropped and the word fallback applies. A path wholly inside the window is found
        (second feed: 1000 x "a" then " /usr/lib/x " then 1000 x "a" separated by spaces; click on "lib" selects "/usr/lib/x").
        Alternative: accept the truncated match.
cite:   S5 in the issue; iTerm2 uses a +-10 line radius (smartSelectionRadius) instead, no character bound.

### SS-C5b/c/d  (the window edge inside a long C++ name, on a `:`)  [D-WINDOW, review of #47]
size:   70x200, one logical line
feed:   b: "a::" x 4000 (12000 chars), click char 6000; c: "a::" x 2000 + "a" + " x" x 100, click char 5895 (the window starts on
        the second `:` of a "a::", 5895 - 4096 = 1799); d: "a::" x 4000, click char 3001 (the window ends on a first `:`, 3001 + 4095)
sel:    what a word double-click selects there (the `a` or the `::`), not the 8188-character C++ name the regex finds inside the window
note:   a match the rule finds may start (end) a character or two inside the window when the edge falls on a character the rule cannot
        start (end) with, so "touching the edge" is not enough: a match starting (ending) in the run of non-blank characters at an edge
        where the line goes on is dropped. Wholly inside the window ("x " + "a::" x 1000 + "a y") the 3001-character name is selected.
        A rule matching across blanks (quoted strings) can still pair up differently in the window than on the whole line.
cite:   rust-critic #47 round 1 B2 (the "a::" x 4000 repro)

### SS-C5e  (a window start edge with no blank in it, the window ending with the line)  [#351 r2 n1]
size:   70x200, one logical line
feed:   "a/" x 3000 (6000 chars, no blank), click char 5000 (the window is chars 904..6000: it ends with the line, starts
        mid-path, and holds no blank)
sel:    the word: the whole line, as a word double-click selects it; not the 5096-character path the rule finds in the window
note:   with no blank in the window, the run at its start edge is the whole window, so every match in it may be the tail
        of a longer one and none is taken
cite:   SS-C5b..d; rust-critic #47 round 2 n1

### SS-C6  (latency, release test)
size:   1x2048 full of "/a" repeated, 64 rules (the 12 defaults + 52 copies with distinct patterns)
click:  middle
bound:  double-click handling <= 5 ms wall time on the release build (issue done-list). Regex crate guarantees linear time; the
        cost is 64 scans of <= 8192 chars. Recompile of 64 patterns must NOT happen per click (compile at config load).
cite:   issue #47 done-list; regex crate docs (no backtracking)

## 5. trim_trailing_whitespace  (default true).  Mechanism: App::selection_text / rich copy.
# Existing behaviour (extract() in selection.rs): on every logical line the cells AFTER its last non-blank cell are never
# emitted, and trailing '\n' of the whole text is trimmed. That is today's `trim = true` and must stay byte-identical.
# `blank` = a cell with ch == ' ' and no flags other than PAD/LINK (is_blank): styles (erased coloured cells) do NOT make it
# non-blank; U+00A0 and U+3000 are NOT blank (they are content). Wide-char SPACER and PAD cells are never emitted in either mode.
# trim = false  : on every row up to the row holding the LAST non-blank cell of the selection, emit the blanks up to the
#                 selection's last column on that row (full width for non-final rows). Rows after that last non-blank row
#                 are still dropped (so a select-all does not append a screen of blank lines). Soft-wrapped rows never trimmed
#                 or padded differently: the wrap hides the newline and the blanks are mid-line content in both modes.
# iTerm2: advanced setting TrimWhitespaceOnCopy (default true), https://iterm2.com/documentation/2.1/documentation-hidden-settings.html
#         (old docs: `defaults write com.googlecode.iterm2 TrimWhitespaceOnCopy -bool false`). Exact current key not confirmed.

### TR-1  size 3x10   feed "ab\r\ncd"   begin (0,0) char, extend (1,9)
trim=true : "ab\ncd"
trim=false: "ab        \ncd        "         # row0 padded to col 9, row1 padded to the selection end col 9
cite: extract() text_end rule; this fixture's trim=false definition

### TR-2  size 3x10   feed "ab"   begin (0,0), extend (0,4)
trim=true : "ab"
trim=false: "ab   "                           # cols 0-4

### TR-3  (soft wrap: blanks before a wrap are content)    size 4x5   feed "abc  def"    # row0 "abc  " wrapped, row1 "def"
select all
trim=true : "abc  def"
trim=false: "abc  def  "        # CORRECTED in #47: was "abc  def"; select all ends at (1,4), and row 1 is padded to
                               # the selection end column like TR-9 (D-TRIMALL)
cite: extract(): `n < end && !line.wrapped` => newline only on hard line ends

### TR-4  (blanks at the end of a wrapped line's last row)   size 4x5   feed "abcdefg"+"   "   # row0 "abcde" wrapped, row1 "fg   "
begin (0,0), extend (1,4)
trim=true : "abcdefg"
trim=false: "abcdefg   "

### TR-5  (wide char that did not fit: PAD cell)   size 4x5   feed "abcd日"   # c4 of row0 = PAD, 日 on row1 c0-1
begin (0,0), extend (1,4)
trim=true : "abcd日"                          # PAD is not a space and not emitted
trim=false: "abcd日   "                       # row1: 日 + 3 blanks (c2-c4); SPACER c1 not emitted
cite: extract() `cell.is_spacer() || cell.is_pad()`

### TR-6  (non-blank space-like scalars are content)   size 2x10   feed "a\u{a0}"  / "b\u{3000}"
trim=true : "a\u{a0}"    and  "b\u{3000}"     # kept: not ' '
cite: is_blank only ' '

### TR-7  (erased coloured cells are blank)   size 2x10   feed "ab\e[41m   \e[0m"   # 3 red-background blanks after ab
begin (0,0), extend (0,4)
trim=true : "ab"
trim=false: "ab   "
rich(trim=true):  no run for the blanks (the red background is trimmed with them);  rich(trim=false): the 3 blanks carry background-color
cite: is_blank ignores styles; D-TRIMSTYLE

### TR-8  (block selection trims/pads each row to the block's right edge)   size 3x10  feed "ab\r\ncdef"  block (0,0)-(1,3)
trim=true : "ab\ncdef"
trim=false: "ab  \ncdef"

### TR-9  (blank tail rows are never padded)   size 5x10  feed "ab"  select all
trim=true : "ab"
trim=false: "ab        "        # DECISION D-TRIMALL: output ends at the last non-blank row; that row is padded to the selection end col (9).
                               # Rows 1-4 (all blank) are dropped in both modes.

## 6. COPY SEMANTICS
# - Copy (plain): public.utf8-plain-text only (NSPasteboardTypeString). Today's behaviour, subject to trim_trailing_whitespace.
# - Copy with Formatting: ONE pasteboard write (single clearContents + declare) of three types: public.rtf, public.html and
#   public.utf8-plain-text, the plain string byte-identical to what Copy would write. Consumers pick: TextEdit/Pages prefer RTF,
#   Mail and browsers HTML, terminals/editors plain text.
# - iTerm2: Edit > Copy with Styles, docs (menu items) https://iterm2.com/3.5/documentation-menu-items.html ; it writes RTF
#   (public.rtf) per the third-party note https://also.github.io/notes/2016/03/19/copy-terminal-html.html. Terminal.app copies
#   RTF + plain by default; NOT verified (closed source, no binary used): treat as unverified; lead's manual check (ls --color
#   -> TextEdit and Mail) is the arbiter. HTML is Tessera-specific.
# - Disabled (validateMenuItem) when there is no selection. No selection => returns None, pasteboard untouched.
# - Rich output above the 16 MiB cap => None for the rich types; the plain copy proceeds (section 8).
# - Styles come from the cell's resolved style: indexed colours through the live theme palette to #RRGGBB, truecolor as is,
#   Default fg/bg => NO colour property (inherit from the paste target: DECISION D-DEFCOLOUR). Inverse swaps resolved fg/bg
#   (default colours resolve to the theme's foreground/background and are then written, since a swap is not inheritable).
#   bold -> bold, italic -> italic, any underline style -> single underline, strikethrough -> line-through. Faint, blink,
#   conceal, overline: no output (conceal text still copied: the plain copy contains it too, D-CONCEAL).
# - OSC 8 / detected links: text only, never <a> or \field (D10).

## 7. OUTPUT GRAMMAR
### 7a HTML  (the ONLY elements: html head meta body pre span; the ONLY attribute: style; no <a>, <img>, <link>, <script>, url(), @import)
document := "<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset=\"utf-8\"></head><body><pre style=\"font-family:Menlo,monospace\">" "\n" body "</pre></body></html>"
# the LF after the <pre> open tag is always written (#351): a parser drops one LF right after it, so a body starting
# with a blank line keeps that line
body     := (run | "\n")*                 # lines joined by a literal LF, no trailing LF; <pre> keeps spaces
run      := text | "<span style=\"" decl (";" decl)* "\">" text "</span>"
decl     := "color:#rrggbb" | "background-color:#rrggbb" | "font-weight:bold" | "font-style:italic"
          | "text-decoration:underline" | "text-decoration:line-through" | "text-decoration:underline line-through"
# declaration ORDER is fixed: color, background-color, font-weight, font-style, text-decoration. Hex is lowercase, 6 digits.
# Adjacent cells with an identical resolved style merge into one run; a run with no declaration is bare text (no span).
# The font family is the constant `Menlo,monospace`: the configured font name is not interpolated (nothing config- or
# child-derived reaches an attribute value; D-FONT).
escape(c) for every scalar c of the cell text (cluster scalars included):
    '&' -> "&amp;"   '<' -> "&lt;"   '>' -> "&gt;"   '"' -> "&quot;"   "'" -> "&#39;"
    '\' -> "&#92;"   '{' -> "&#123;"  '}' -> "&#125;"      (not required in HTML; escaped anyway so one rule serves both formats)
    any scalar > U+007E (incl. U+007F..U+009F, NBSP, ZWJ, bidi controls, astral) -> "&#x" lowercase-hex "no leading zeros" ";"
    C0 controls except LF (0x00-0x09, 0x0B-0x1F) and DEL -> DROPPED (nothing emitted)
    everything else (printable ASCII 0x20-0x7E, minus the list above) -> itself
cite: HTML Living Standard 13.3 serialising text/attribute values https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#serialising-html-fragments ;
      OWASP XSS prevention rule 1/2 (escape & < > " ').

### 7b RTF  (RTF Specification 1.9.1, Microsoft: https://www.loc.gov/preservation/digital/formats/fdd/fdd000473.shtml and
###          https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=10725 ; no \pict, \field, \object, \*\ extensions, \info)
document := "{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0\fmodern Menlo;}}" colortbl "\f0\fs24 " body "}"
colortbl := "{\colortbl;" ("\red" N "\green" N "\blue" N ";")* "}"     # entry 0 = auto (the leading ';'); entries 1.. in first-use order,
                                                                        # deduplicated, fg and bg share the table
body     := (run | "\par ")*      # LF => "\par " (control word + ONE delimiter space)
run      := text | "{" ("\cf" k " ")? ("\cb" k " ")? ("\b ")? ("\i ")? ("\ul ")? ("\strike ")? text "}"
# EVERY control word is followed by exactly one space (the delimiter); a literal space that starts the text after it is a second
# space, so it is preserved. Groups scope the attributes, so no \b0 / \ulnone resets are needed.
# Table cap: at most 4096 distinct colours (more => rich copy refused, same as the size cap; D-COLCAP).
escape(c):
    '\' -> "\\"   '{' -> "\{"   '}' -> "\}"
    scalar > U+007E, BMP  -> "\u" signed16(code) "?"           e.g. U+00E9 -> \u233?   U+65E5 -> ☈5?   U+301 -> \u769?
        signed16: code <= 32767 ? code : code - 65536          e.g. U+F8FF -> \u-1793?
    astral -> two \u items, one per UTF-16 surrogate, each followed by "?"      U+1F600 -> \u-10179?\u-8704?
    C0 controls except LF, DEL -> DROPPED
    '?' after \uN is the ANSI fallback and is consumed by \uc1 (the default); so `\u233?` followed by text "x" is "éx".
    all other ASCII (0x20-0x7E) -> itself
# Why signed: RTF 1.9.1 "Unicode" section: \uN with N a signed 16-bit decimal.

### 7c ROWS  (input cells -> expected strings; colours given as resolved #rrggbb)
### RT-1 plain                    cells: "hi"
html: <!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"></head><body><pre style="font-family:Menlo,monospace">\nhi</pre>        (\n = one LF byte)</body></html>
rtf:  {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0\fmodern Menlo;}}{\colortbl;}\f0\fs24 hi}
### RT-2 red bold then newline     cells: line1 "a" fg #ff0000 bold ; line2 "b" default
html body: <span style="color:#ff0000;font-weight:bold">a</span>\nb          (\n = one LF byte)
rtf:  {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0\fmodern Menlo;}}{\colortbl;\red255\green0\blue0;}\f0\fs24 {\cf1 \b a}\par b}
### RT-3 hostile text              cells: <script>&"'\{}é😀   (plain style)
html body: &lt;script&gt;&amp;&quot;&#39;&#92;&#123;&#125;&#xe9;&#x1f600;
rtf body:  <script>&"'\\\{\}\u233?\u-10179?\u-8704?
    # must hold: the HTML body contains no '<' except the fixed wrapper tags, no unescaped & " ', and no scalar > 0x7E; the RTF body has
    # no unescaped \ { } and no byte > 0x7E. The test feeds every scalar 0x00-0xFF and a sample of astral/bidi/ZWJ scalars.
### RT-4 colours and decorations   cells: "x" fg #00ff00 bg #0000ff italic underline
html body: <span style="color:#00ff00;background-color:#0000ff;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline">x</span>
rtf body:  {\cf1 \cb2 \i \ul x}     colortbl: {\colortbl;\red0\green255\blue0;\red0\green0\blue255;}
### RT-5 merge and split          cells: "ab" fg #ff0000 ; "c" fg #ff0000 bold
html body: <span style="color:#ff0000">ab</span><span style="color:#ff0000;font-weight:bold">c</span>
rtf body:  {\cf1 ab}{\cf1 \b c}    (colour 1 reused)
### RT-6 strike + underline        cells: "z" underline strikethrough
html body: <span style="text-decoration:underline line-through">z</span>        rtf body: {\ul \strike z}
### RT-7 leading space after a control word   cells: "a" then " b" in bold ("a" plain)
rtf body:  a{\b  b}                  # first space = delimiter, second = the literal blank
### RT-8 controls dropped         cells: "a" ESC "b" BEL "c" U+0085 "d"     (the grid never holds LF in a cell, but may hold these)
html body: abc&#x85;d             # ESC (0x1b) and BEL (0x07) dropped; U+0085 > 0x7E is escaped, not dropped
rtf body:  abc\u133?d
### RT-9 clusters and wide        cells: "e" + U+0301 ; 日 (wide, spacer skipped)
html body: e&#x301;&#x65e5;           rtf body: e\u769?☈5?
### RT-10 OSC 8 link text         cells: "link" with a hyperlink id            html/rtf: plain run "link" (no <a>, no \field)
### RT-11 trimmed styled blanks   see TR-7
### RT-12 inverse                 cells: "i" fg Default bg Default, inverse; theme fg #c0c0c0 bg #101010
html body: <span style="color:#101010;background-color:#c0c0c0">i</span>   # swap of the resolved theme colours
### RT-13 empty selection         no cells => None (no pasteboard write), also when trim removes everything (all blanks)

## 8. S5 BOUNDS
# MAX_SMART_RULES = 64: the 65th rule is dropped with a warning (config load), defaults count towards it? DECISION D-RULECOUNT: user rules only; with
#   include-defaults the sum is capped at 64. Test: 65 rules => 64 kept and one warning.
# pattern <= 1024 bytes (1025 refused with a warning); compile with regex::RegexBuilder size_limit(1 MiB) and dfa_size_limit(1 MiB);
#   nest_limit(50). A pattern that fails to compile is skipped with a warning, other rules still work.
# empty-match patterns (`a*`, `^`) are refused at load: a rule must not match the empty string (test on the string "").
# scanned logical line <= 8192 characters around the click (section 4 SS-C5).
# rich output <= 16 MiB = 16_777_216 bytes per string (html and rtf each): exactly the cap passes, one byte more => rich refused, plain copy
#   still written. Generation aborts as soon as a string exceeds the cap (no unbounded String growth); the test uses a lowered cap constant.
#   The styled runs collected under the terminal lock are bounded by the same cap: each run with a look of its own is charged the least
#   HTML markup it needs (an empty span and `color:#rrggbb`, 35 bytes) on top of its text, so the collection stops once that lower bound
#   of the HTML passes 16 MiB (a cell-by-cell colour flood stops after about 466 k runs, not 16 M).
#   Worst-case growth per cell: html `<span style="color:#rrggbb;background-color:#rrggbb;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline line-through">` (~150 B)
#   + `&#x10ffff;` (10 B) vs 1 B of text, so a 100 k-cell selection can reach the cap with hostile styling.
# colours table <= 4096 entries.
# Patterns are user config (trusted-ish) but MATCHED TEXT is child-controlled: never shown in UI (S3), never evaluated; only used as a span.

## 9. DECISIONS FOR THE MILESTONE LEAD (recommended option first)
# D-GESTURE   Issue says double-click selects the smart match. iTerm2 default is QUAD-click; double-click only with the pref
#             "Double-click performs smart selection". Recommend: follow the issue (double-click), plus a `[selection] smart_double_click = true`
#             switch if cheap; triple-click stays the logical line (no change).
# D-NOWORDRULE Do NOT ship iTerm2's `\S+` low rule (changes every existing word test). Without it no default rule is a catch-all.
# D-URLRULE   http_url: single-alternative regex + url.rs U4/U5 post-trim, or call url::url_at (U1-U9: also ftp/file/IRIs). Recommend the
#             regex rule with the post-trim so the config keeps one mechanism; keep url.rs behaviour for cmd-click untouched.
# D-URLTRAIL  Click ON a stripped trailing '.' still selects the (trimmed) URL: coverage on the untrimmed match (SS-U4b).
# D-TIE       Tie-break order: precision, length, start, rule index (iTerm2: undefined).
# D-EMAILTLD  iTerm2's email rule caps the TLD at 4 letters ({2,4}); `x@y.museum` then falls to the include_path rule and selects `y.museum`
#             (SS-E2). Recommend {2,24}? That diverges from iTerm2 but selects what users expect. Fixture row SS-E2 follows iTerm2 {2,4}; flip it with the decision.
# D-IPV6      Zone ids / v4-mapped tails unsupported; ports excluded from ipv4/ipv6 (SS-I3/I4/I5).
# D-WINDOW    Truncated candidates at a window edge are dropped (SS-C5).
# D-DEFCOLOUR Default fg/bg emit no colour so Mail/TextEdit keep their own; alternative is to write the theme colours (matches iTerm2 look,
#             breaks dark themes pasted onto white pages).
# D-FONT      Constant `Menlo,monospace` / `\fs24`; configured font and size are not interpolated.
# D-TRIMSTYLE trim also removes coloured blank cells in rich copy (consistent with plain).
# D-TRIMALL   trim=false pads only rows up to the last non-blank row (TR-9).
# D-CONCEAL   Concealed text is copied like the plain copy does.
# D-COLCAP    More than 4096 distinct colours => rich refused.
# D-RULECOUNT 64 caps the user's list; defaults are separate unless `smart_rules` replaces them (recommend: unset = defaults, set = replaces; an
#             `include_defaults = true` key is optional).
# D-PRIORITY  The issue says "regex + priority". Recommend priority = iTerm2's five named levels (very_low .. very_high), score = weight x length
#             (not a plain integer priority: a plain integer would let a short very-high rule hide the longer correct match). Config row:
#             smart_rules = [{ name = "...", pattern = "...", precision = "normal" }].
#
# ISSUE TEXT CORRECTIONS
# 1. "iTerm2-like defaults: ... hashes, IPv4/IPv6": iTerm2's default set (11 rules, plist) has NO hash, IPv4 or IPv6 rule, no single-quote rule,
#    and no Rust-compatible lookbehind; those three are Tessera additions (section 2).
# 2. "highest-priority rule match": iTerm2 does not take the highest precision class outright: score = weight x length, one level = 1000x.
#    A longer lower-level match outranks a shorter higher-level one only when it is >1000x longer, which cannot happen inside a 8192-char
#    window between adjacent levels (normal vs high needs 1000+ chars, so it can; very_high vs normal needs 1,000,000). Recommend
#    implementing weight x length exactly (cheap) rather than "class first".
# 3. "double-click": see D-GESTURE.
# 4. Today's selection text already drops blanks after the last non-blank cell of every logical line (extract()), so trim_trailing_whitespace=true
#    is a no-op; the new work is trim=false (padding), not trim=true.
# 5. `regex.workspace` must have `unicode-perl`/`unicode-gencat` features for \b and \p{L}; default features suffice. No lookaround anywhere.

## 10. SOURCES
# iTerm2 Smart Selection docs: https://iterm2.com/documentation-smart-selection.html
# iTerm2 default rules: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnachman/iTerm2/master/plists/SmartSelectionRules.plist
# iTerm2 scoring: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnachman/iTerm2/master/sources/ContentAnalysis/iTermTextExtractor.m (smartSelectionAt) and
#                 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnachman/iTerm2/master/sources/Settings/SmartSelectionController.m (precision weights)
# iTerm2 pointer prefs: https://iterm2.com/3.3/documentation-preferences-pointer.html ; menu items https://iterm2.com/3.5/documentation-menu-items.html
# iTerm2 hidden settings (TrimWhitespaceOnCopy): https://iterm2.com/documentation/2.1/documentation-hidden-settings.html
# RTF 1.9.1: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=10725 ; HTML serialisation: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#serialising-html-fragments
